games.title: Tense Tower
games.skillName: Choosing verb tenses, like the present perfect and past progressive
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to develop their understanding of the concepts set out in English Appendix 2 by: use of the present perfect form of verbs instead of the simple past [for example, He has gone out to play contrasted with He went out to play]
games.instruction: Read the sentence, then tap the verb that fits.
games.hint: Not quite. Ask yourself when it happened and whether it matters now, then try again.

questions.ask: Which is the present perfect? 'She ___ out to play.'
What is the simple past of 'go'?
'I ___ my homework, so now I can play.'
'Yesterday, we ___ a film.'
'He was running.' Which tense is this?
'They have eaten.' Which tense is this?
'Look out of the window! It ___ right now.'
Which sentence uses the present perfect?
'When the bell rang, we ___ lunch.'
Pick the present perfect of 'write': 'She ___ a letter.'

games.title: Clause Castle
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to use and understand the grammatical terminology in English Appendix 2 accurately and appropriately when discussing their writing and reading (clause, subordinate clause); express time, place and cause using conjunctions [for example, when, before, after, while, so, because]
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Look for the verb and the word that starts the clause, then try again.

questions.ask: A clause must contain a ___.
Which of these is a clause?
Which of these is NOT a clause?
'I ate lunch because I was hungry.' Find the subordinate clause.
'When the bell rang, we went in.' Find the subordinate clause.
A subordinate clause ___ make sense on its own.
Which word often starts a subordinate clause?
'We played out after it stopped raining.' Find the main clause.
How many clauses are in 'I sang and Mia danced.'?
Which conjunction starts a subordinate clause? 'Wash your hands ___ you eat.'

games.title: Dictionary Dash
games.skillName: Using a dictionary to find meanings
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to develop positive attitudes to reading and understanding of what they read by: using dictionaries to check the meaning of words that they have read

games.title: Book Explorer
games.skillName: Non-fiction, poetry forms, myths and legends
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to retrieve and record information from non-fiction; discuss words and phrases that capture the reader's interest and imagination; recognise some different forms of poetry [for example, free verse, narrative poetry]; increase their familiarity with a wide range of books, including fairy stories, myths and legends, and retell some of these orally
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
